characteristics.cultivar: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis and hybrids
characteristics.teaware: Teapot, excellent with or without milk

description.short: Aromatic, gently brisk southern Indian black tea, sharing its crisp brightness with Ceylon teas
description.overview: The sole major tea region of southern India, situated high in the Western Ghats. Due to equatorial proximity, tea is harvested year-round without the marked seasonal flushes seen in Assam and Darjeeling.
description.taste: Aromatic, pleasantly brisk, briskly refreshing, and lighter than Assam
description.processing: Plucking → withering → rolling (orthodox or CTC) → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: Plantations in the Nilgiri hills were established by British colonists in the mid-19th century, shortly following early successes in Assam and Darjeeling.
history.development: Thanks to equatorial latitudes and high altitude, Nilgiri avoids cold winter dormancy; bushes produce fresh leaves throughout all 12 months.
history.modern: Nilgiri is frequently compared in brightness and crisp astringency to Ceylon teas of nearby Sri Lanka, which shares similar geographical and climatic influences.
interestingFacts: The name 'Nilgiri' translates to 'Blue Mountains' in Sanskrit and Tamil, named for the hazy blue mist that cloaks the peaks at dawn.
Nilgiri is the only prominent high-volume tea-growing region in Southern India, whereas northeastern states (Assam, West Bengal) dominate the rest of the country.
